questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(6,0,2)$ and $B(1,1,3)$, and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨3,1,-2⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). We already have one vector $v=⟨3,1,-2⟩.$ Let's also use the displacement vector $\overset{\to }{AB}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,1,3⟩-⟨6,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-5,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $a=⟨6,0,2⟩$ of the point $A,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =a+sv+t\overset{\to }{AB} \\ r & =⟨6,0,2⟩+s⟨3,1,-2⟩+t⟨-5,1,1⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 23 \\ 14\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-3,5,4⟩$ and $w=⟨4,7,-1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 7 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-33i+13j-41k \\  & =⟨-33,13,-41⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-33,13,-41⟩.$

questions.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=⟨0,8,-1⟩+t⟨-1,1,7⟩+s⟨3,-5,1⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-1,1,7⟩$ and $w=⟨3,-5,1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 1 & 7 \\ 3 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =36i+22j+2k \\  & =⟨36,22,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨36,22,2⟩.$

questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $P(3,6,2),\,Q(2,-9,0)$, and $R(3,0,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). Let's use the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨2,-9,0⟩-⟨3,6,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-15,-2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =⟨3,0,1⟩-⟨3,6,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-6,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $p=⟨3,6,2⟩$ of the point $P,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+s\overset{\to }{PQ}+t\overset{\to }{PR} \\ r & =⟨3,6,2⟩+s⟨-1,-15,-2⟩+t⟨0,-6,-1⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $B(1,5,13)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨-7,12,5⟩+s⟨-2,4,1⟩$ and $r=⟨-9,21,2⟩+t⟨2,5,-3⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨-2,4,1⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨2,5,-3⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $B(1,5,13)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $b=⟨1,5,13⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =b+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨1,5,13⟩+s⟨-2,4,1⟩+t⟨2,5,-3⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
